title: bug: the guest session stamps no execution identity on qa_approve/qa_reject, so a VM QA seat can never decide a verified-local task
description:
Found by CQ-V12's whole-epic review (task-b621ddc9, worker-0e1ab990, 2026-11-01). This fails closed, so it is NOT a gate bypass. It does block the QA half of verified-local activation.

Defect:
- scripts/local-runner/guest-session.mjs:32 STAMPED adds the host identity to only four tools: moe.get_context (sessionId), moe.start_step, moe.complete_step and moe.complete_task (attemptId, generation, sessionId).
- CQ-V06 changed the requirement. Under verified-local, moe.qa_approve and moe.qa_reject need QA's own attemptId, generation and served-context sessionId (delivery/reviewBinding.ts assertReviewBinding → STEP_ENTRY_IDENTITY_REQUIRED). CQ-V06a (task-a4ad3fdb) made moe-proxy stamp them (packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts:337).
- Nothing on the guest path can supply them. scripts/local-runner/guest-bridge.mjs TOOLS.qa admits only summary/candidateId, and FORBIDDEN_IDENTITY_KEYS refuses attemptId/generation from the guest. So every VM QA decision on a strict task is refused.
- CQ-M07j1 (task-c7cead1b) assumes STAMPED "mirrors what moe-proxy does on /mcp".

Repro: scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs H3 (line ~774). With the QA binding, the forwarded moe.qa_approve/moe.qa_reject args carry taskId and workerId but no attemptId, generation or sessionId. H3's `stamps` map pins that today.

Failing-test sketch: add 'moe.qa_approve': execution and 'moe.qa_reject': execution to H3's stamps map. It fails on today's code.

Fix:
- Add both tools to STAMPED with EXECUTION, from the frozen host binding and the session's sessionId, never from guest args.
- Refresh the "only onto tools whose daemon schema accepts it" comment.
- Keep FORBIDDEN_IDENTITY_KEYS unchanged.
definitionOfDone: guest-session.mjs stamps attemptId, generation and sessionId onto moe.qa_approve and moe.qa_reject from the host binding and session id, never from guest arguments
local-runner-bridge.test.mjs H3 pins the QA stamps and fails without the fix; a guest-supplied attemptId/generation/sessionId is still refused (BRIDGE_IDENTITY_MISMATCH / BRIDGE_ARGUMENT_DENIED)
node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs passes, and any doc naming the guest-stamped tools matches the code

implementationPlan.description:
1. Red test first, then the fix (DoD 1-2).

TEST, in scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs H3 (~line 775). Add 'moe.qa_approve': execution and 'moe.qa_reject': execution to the `stamps` map. The QA binding's loop already forwards every TOOLS.qa tool, so H3 must fail on today's code: the forwarded args lack attemptId, generation and sessionId. Run `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs` once to SEE it fail before the fix.

Add QA-binding refusal rows to H3's denied part. Use a second session, `openSession(proc2, { binding: QA })`, because the existing denied session uses the worker BINDING, where moe.qa_approve is BRIDGE_TOOL_DENIED.
- moe.qa_approve with { attemptId: QA.attemptId } and with { generation: QA.generation }: BRIDGE_IDENTITY_MISMATCH. guest-bridge.mjs FORBIDDEN_IDENTITY_KEYS covers both, even with equal values.
- moe.qa_reject with { attemptId: 'attempt-9' }: BRIDGE_IDENTITY_MISMATCH.
- moe.qa_approve and moe.qa_reject with { sessionId: SESSION_ID }: BRIDGE_ARGUMENT_DENIED. sessionId is not in TOOLS.qa's allowed keys.
Assert that run.forwarded is [] and that each reply is refused(id, code).

FIX, in scripts/local-runner/guest-session.mjs:32. STAMPED gains 'moe.qa_approve': EXECUTION and 'moe.qa_reject': EXECUTION. reply() already takes the values only from the frozen binding (attemptId, generation) and the session's validated sessionId (`identity`), and stamps them after scopeRequest. A guest can therefore never supply them: scopeRequest refuses those keys first.
Refresh the comment above STAMPED: host identity is stamped after scoping onto exactly the tools whose daemon schema takes it, the same six tools moe-proxy's EXECUTION_IDENTITY_TOOLS stamps (packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts). qa_approve and qa_reject need it under verified-local (delivery/reviewBinding.ts).
Keep FORBIDDEN_IDENTITY_KEYS, TOOLS and scopeRequest in guest-bridge.mjs unchanged.

Error handling is unchanged: a refused scope is still one fixed-code reply that never reaches forward, and a daemon refusal of the stamped call is still BRIDGE_UPSTREAM_FAILED. Do not add a guest-side schema field to guest-mcp-tools.json either: the guest never presents identity.
implementationPlan.note: Red run of H3 before the fix: deepEqual of run.forwarded failed for the QA binding — moe.qa_approve/moe.qa_reject args lacked attemptId 'attempt-1', generation 2, sessionId. After STAMPED fix + QA refusal rows: H3 passes. Dirty peer paths left untouched.

implementationPlan.description:
2. Docs that name the stamped tools (DoD 3). Keep each edit to the lines named here. Both docs are also declared by open docs/integration rows, so write them with the Edit tool and touch nothing else.
(a) docs/MCP_SERVER.md, the paragraph 'Execution identity over moe-proxy (CQ-F09, CQ-F12a, CQ-V06a)' (~line 326). Add one sentence: on a VM seat the host guest session (scripts/local-runner/guest-session.mjs) stamps the same fields onto the same six tools, from its frozen binding and its session id, after scoping; a guest that presents attemptId or generation is refused BRIDGE_IDENTITY_MISMATCH, and one that presents sessionId is refused BRIDGE_ARGUMENT_DENIED.
(b) docs/CONFIGURATION.md, rows `MOE_SESSION_ID` (~line 44) and `MOE_ATTEMPT_ID` / `MOE_ATTEMPT_GENERATION` (~line 45). Their tool lists predate CQ-V06a. Add `moe.qa_approve` and `moe.qa_reject` so both rows match packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts EXECUTION_IDENTITY_TOOLS and docs/MCP_SERVER.md.
Then grep docs/, packages/moe-proxy/README.md and scripts/CLAUDE.md for any other list of stamped tools, and fix only a list that is wrong.
implementationPlan.note: One sentence in MCP_SERVER.md; two CONFIGURATION.md rows. Other stamped-tool lists (proxy README, scripts/CLAUDE.md) already correct.

implementationPlan.description:
3. One verification gate, run once at the end, from the repo root, in place (node test files only; nothing is built). The exact command:
`node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-agents.test.mjs`

Self-review by inspection of reply(): scopeRequest refuses guest identity keys before the stamp; the stamp overwrites from the frozen binding + session id; worker role stays BRIDGE_TOOL_DENIED on qa tools (existing denied row); forward receives args verbatim. No fix needed.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: A VM QA seat's moe.qa_approve and moe.qa_reject leave the host guest session carrying attemptId and generation from the frozen host binding and sessionId from the session, exactly as moe-proxy stamps them for a host seat. A guest still cannot present any of the three.
acceptanceCriteria: H3: with the QA binding, the forwarded moe.qa_approve and moe.qa_reject args equal {taskId, workerId, attemptId, generation, sessionId} from the binding and session. The test fails on the pre-fix code.
H3: under the QA binding, a guest attemptId or generation on either qa tool is BRIDGE_IDENTITY_MISMATCH and a guest sessionId is BRIDGE_ARGUMENT_DENIED, with nothing forwarded.
Docs that list the stamped tools name all six, including qa_approve and qa_reject, and MCP_SERVER.md names the guest session.
invariants: The identity comes only from the frozen host binding and the session id, never from guest args.
guest-bridge.mjs FORBIDDEN_IDENTITY_KEYS, TOOLS and scopeRequest are unchanged.
A worker-role session still cannot call the qa tools.
compatibility: Legacy and observe daemons fence an optional presented identity, as they do for moe-proxy's stamps, so nothing changes for a legacy task.
CQ-M07j1's seatForward relays the stamped args verbatim.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. Letting the guest present the identity: rejected. It is caller-minted evidence, and guest-bridge.mjs FORBIDDEN_IDENTITY_KEYS exists to refuse exactly that.
2. Stamping inside guest-bridge.mjs scopeRequest: rejected. scopeRequest holds no sessionId, and guest-session.mjs reply() is already the single place where host identity is stamped after scoping.
3. A daemon-side exemption for VM QA: rejected. It would weaken CQ-V06's review binding.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- guest-session.mjs reply() stamps `{attemptId: binding.attemptId, generation: binding.generation, sessionId}` onto STAMPED[tool], after scopeRequest.
- moe-proxy's EXECUTION_IDENTITY_TOOLS (packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts ~line 332) stamps get_context (session) and start_step/complete_step/complete_task/qa_approve/qa_reject (attempt+session).
- TOOLS.qa allows only summary/candidateId on qa_approve, and reason/failedDodItems/issues/candidateId on qa_reject.
- FORBIDDEN_IDENTITY_KEYS = role, attemptId, generation, processStartedAt, host. sessionId is refused as BRIDGE_ARGUMENT_DENIED because no qa entry allows it.
- H3 iterates the tools of [BINDING, QA] with `stamps[tool]`; its denied list runs on the worker binding.
- No open plan declares guest-session.mjs, guest-bridge.mjs or local-runner-bridge.test.mjs (checked 2026-11-01).
- CI runs the bridge test in the local-runner node --test line.
planningNotes.risks:
- docs/MCP_SERVER.md is declared by open rows WT-17 and CQ-M06, and docs/CONFIGURATION.md by WT-17, WT-19, CQ-M06, CQ-RF07 and task-76ae5c47. Edit them with Edit only, so they land under skip-untouched. A peer mid-step on the same doc can hold the path (MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_EDITING) until it finishes.
- local-runner-agents.test.mjs reads the daemon's dist read-only; never build in place.
